course.title: ISBD Cataloguing Competency
course.description: A 44-lesson path with 112 scored exercises in MARC21, ISBD reasoning, safe automation, and professional cataloguer judgment, sequenced from foundation to independent assessment.

onboarding.title: Welcome to ISBD Training
onboarding.body: Learn how bibliographic records are structured, how ISBD punctuation works, and how to review automated cataloguing suggestions safely.

onboarding.title: How much cataloguing experience do you have?
How training works
onboarding.body: Learn → See → Try → Check → Understand → Practice → Master. Completion records activity; mastery requires successful, unassisted practice.

glossary.definition: A standard for representing bibliographic and authority data in machine-readable fields.
A three-character number identifying a MARC field and its bibliographic role.
One of two field positions whose value changes how a MARC field is interpreted or displayed.
A coded component within a MARC variable field, such as 245$a for title proper.
International Standard Bibliographic Description, which organizes descriptive elements and their presentation.
Punctuation that expresses the relationship between ISBD descriptive elements.
The chief title of a resource, normally transcribed in 245$a.
A subtitle or other information subordinate to the title proper, normally in 245$b.
A statement naming persons or bodies responsible for the resource, normally in 245$c.
A statement identifying an edition, normally transcribed in field 250.
The number and type of physical units, normally recorded in 300$a.
Use of controlled, verified forms for names, subjects, and other access points.
Recording descriptive information from the prescribed source according to cataloguing instructions.
An ISBD grouping of related bibliographic elements, such as title, edition, or publication.

modules.title: Foundations
modules.description: Understand what a bibliographic record describes and where professional judgment begins.
objectives: Apply concepts in staged interactive practice

lessons.title: Records, evidence, and judgment
lessons.why: A record describes a resource from evidence; it is not a log of software actions.
lessons.how: Separate facts transcribed from the source, deterministic presentation rules, and decisions requiring cataloguer judgment.
lessons.common_mistake: Treating a software suggestion as bibliographic evidence.
lessons.do_not_automate: Do not infer a missing source of information or accept an unverified heading.

sections.introduction: Cataloguing begins with evidence about a resource and a structured description of that evidence.
sections.why_it_matters: Reliable records require a clear boundary between transcription, deterministic formatting, and professional judgment.
sections.learn: The assistant may validate known structures. It cannot decide what an ambiguous source says.
sections.see_it: A title page is evidence; a 245 field is a structured representation; punctuation expresses relationships.
sections.reflection: Which parts of your local workflow depend on policy rather than universal rules?

exercises.prompt: What does a bibliographic record primarily describe?
exercises.expected_answer: The resource
hints: Focus on the object being catalogued.
The record represents bibliographic evidence, not software actions.
exercises.explanation: A bibliographic record is a structured description of a resource.

exercises.prompt: A title page is ambiguous about whether a name belongs to the title. Who must decide?
exercises.expected_answer: The cataloguer reviewing the source
hints: Ask whether punctuation alone can resolve the evidence.
Ambiguous transcription remains a human decision.
exercises.explanation: Source-of-information and ambiguous transcription decisions require cataloguer judgment.

exercises.prompt: A vendor record conflicts with the preferred source. What is the defensible action?
options: Retain the source evidence, resolve what the rules determine, and escalate unresolved judgment
Accept the vendor record because it already exists
Let punctuation software choose the facts
exercises.expected_answer: Retain the source evidence, resolve what the rules determine, and escalate unresolved judgment
hints: Focus on the bibliographic role, not the visual appearance.
Compare the supplied evidence with the cataloguing foundations principle.
exercises.explanation: Retain the source evidence, resolve what the rules determine, and escalate unresolved judgment. This follows from the lesson's evidence-first treatment of cataloguing foundations.

lessons.title: Sources of information and faithful transcription
lessons.why: Cataloguers must separate what the resource says from later interpretation.
lessons.how: Work from source evidence, identify the transcription evidence relationship, then make only the supported change.
lessons.common_mistake: Treating transcription evidence as a visual formatting pattern instead of a bibliographic decision.
lessons.do_not_automate: Do not infer ambiguous transcription evidence when the record or source evidence is incomplete.

lessons.title: Anatomy of a MARC field
lessons.why: Punctuation rules act on semantic subfields, while storage still preserves field and subfield occurrences.
lessons.how: Read 245 10 $a as tag 245, indicators 1 and 0, and title-proper subfield a.
lessons.common_mistake: Assuming repeated subfields are interchangeable or that display order can overwrite storage order.
lessons.do_not_automate: Do not reorder meaningful repeated values without a cataloguing rule.

sections.introduction: MARC represents bibliographic roles through fields and coded subfields.
sections.why_it_matters: A correction aimed at the wrong occurrence can damage valid data.
sections.learn: Tags identify fields; indicators qualify meaning; subfield codes identify elements; occurrences identify repetitions.
sections.see_it: 245 10 $a The great Gatsby $b a novel $c F. Scott Fitzgerald
sections.reflection: How would you identify the second 264$a without relying on screen position?

exercises.prompt: Which component contains the statement of responsibility in a typical 245 field?
hints: Look for the subfield role, not its screen position.

exercises.explanation: In a typical MARC21 title statement, 245$c contains the statement of responsibility.

exercises.prompt: Build a 245 field with first indicator 1, second indicator 0, title proper 'Things fall apart', and responsibility 'Chinua Achebe'.
hints: Set both indicators before editing subfields.
Use $a for title proper and $c for responsibility.
The relationship before $c is expressed by a slash.
exercises.explanation: The tag and indicators identify the field, while $a and $c carry distinct bibliographic elements.

modules.title: Title & Responsibility
modules.description: Construct and review semantic relationships in 245 title statements.
objectives: Apply concepts in staged interactive practice

lessons.title: 245 relationship lab
lessons.why: Area 1 punctuation is visible, frequent, and easy to misapply when learned as isolated marks.
lessons.how: Resolve title proper, other title information, and responsibility, then express each boundary once.
lessons.common_mistake: Leaving a period before the responsibility slash or creating duplicate terminal points.
lessons.do_not_automate: Do not choose the title proper from an ambiguous source or rewrite the wording.

sections.introduction: 245$a, $b, and $c form a semantic sequence even when their inputs are not adjacent in the DOM.
sections.why_it_matters: Correct punctuation depends on bibliographic roles and the presence of related elements.
sections.learn: 245$a title proper → colon → 245$b other title information → slash → 245$c responsibility.
sections.see_it: 245 10 $a The great Gatsby : $b a novel / $c F. Scott Fitzgerald.
sections.reflection: Why should the engine inspect whether $c exists before deciding how $b ends?

exercises.prompt: Correct the punctuation without changing the bibliographic information.
hints: Look at the relationship between $a and $b.
$a is title proper; $b is other title information.
Now inspect the relationship between $b and responsibility in $c.
exercises.explanation: The colon expresses the $a-to-$b relationship, the slash introduces responsibility, and the complete statement ends once.

exercises.prompt: Why does the slash appear before 245$c?
exercises.expected_answer: $c contains the statement of responsibility
hints: Identify the role of $c.
The punctuation introduces a bibliographic element.
exercises.explanation: The slash is prescribed because $c introduces the statement of responsibility, not because of its physical position.

exercises.prompt: Find every problem in: 245 10 $a The great Gatsby $b : a novel. $c / F. Scott Fitzgerald..
hints: Check every boundary and the final terminator separately.
One listed colon is the correct title-to-subtitle boundary.
exercises.explanation: $b must not carry an extra period before the responsibility slash, and $c must end with only one point.

options: Evaluate the ordered title elements and each boundary once before changing punctuation
Apply the same suffix to every subfield
exercises.expected_answer: Evaluate the ordered title elements and each boundary once before changing punctuation
hints: Focus on the bibliographic role, not the visual appearance.
Compare the supplied evidence with the terminal punctuation principle.
exercises.explanation: Evaluate the ordered title elements and each boundary once before changing punctuation. This follows from the lesson's evidence-first treatment of terminal punctuation.

lessons.title: Whole-record risk triage

lessons.do_not_automate: Do not infer ambiguous record-level review when the record or source evidence is incomplete.

lessons.title: Practical Assessment capstone
lessons.why: The capstone combines the module's concepts in one evidence-based professional decision.
lessons.how: Review the evidence, separate deterministic changes from judgment, and document any unresolved risk.

lessons.do_not_automate: Do not automate unresolved relationships or authority-sensitive decisions merely to complete the module.
